_comment: The occasion a speech was given, keyed by speech_id. Shown on the report's
share card and available to the report page.
AUTHORED, NEVER DERIVED. 'President + U.S. Capitol + late January' looks
like it implies State of the Union, but that heuristic is wrong for an
inaugural, a farewell, and -- most easily missed -- for a first-year
address, which is formally an Address to a Joint Session of Congress and
NOT a State of the Union. A fact-checking site cannot afford to mislabel
the occasion on its own share card, so each entry is a judgement recorded
by hand.
Trump 2026 IS a State of the Union: his 2025 address was the joint-session
one, and the transcript itself says 'When I last spoke in this chamber 12
months ago'.
A speech_id with no entry simply has no event label; the card omits the
line rather than guessing. Future runs should set this at publish time.
WORDING: spelled out here because the card has no space pressure and the
audience is broad. The short form ('2026 SOTU') is for posts, where 300
characters binds and readers are already politically engaged.
SENATE FLOOR SPEECHES (added 2026-09-01). The event label is the
Congressional Record section heading VERBATIM as printed over the
remarks -- not the granule's outer bill heading, which on the Warren
page is 'PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL...' and governs the
whole page rather than the speech. Each heading was read off the
govinfo.gov Record page recorded in transcript_source_urls below.
A page heading can cover several senators' remarks in sequence; that
is the Record's own structure and is preserved rather than narrowed.
